lesson.title: Property descriptors and shallow freeze
lesson.summary: Return a frozen outer object with own version=1 (enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable) and theme={dark:false}. The nested theme remains mutable. No deep-freeze claim.
explanation: Object.defineProperty(object,name,descriptor) defines an own property and returns that same object. A data descriptor supplies value plus writable, enumerable and configurable flags. Here version is visible to ordinary own-key enumeration, but cannot be assigned a new value or deleted/reconfigured. Omitted flags default to false for a newly defined property.

Object.freeze(object) returns that same object after preventing new own properties and making its own data properties non-writable and non-configurable. It does not recursively freeze a nested object. In this lesson theme still refers to a mutable inner object. A const binding alone would not apply these property restrictions.

Implement the outer frozen settings object while keeping the nested theme object unfrozen. Optional practice: explain why replacing settings.theme and editing settings.theme.dark are different operations.

quiz.question: Which operation can still succeed on the returned object?
choices: settings.theme = {} replaces the frozen outer property
quiz.explanation: Freezing the outer object protects its own property bindings, not the properties of the referenced nested theme.
